title: Securing Elections From AI Deception Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Securing Elections From AI Deception Act is a proposed law aimed at protecting the integrity of elections by limiting the use of AI to create and spread misleading or harmful political content. It would establish safeguards, such as disclosure requirements and penalties, to prevent AI-generated deception from influencing voters or compromising election processes.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that Congress must refuse to provide any additional funds or exceptional regulatory support to companies or financial institutions facing insolvency or financial collapse due to exposures to acute stress within the artificial intelligence market and must provide support to all harmed Americans instead.
action: Referred to the Committee on Financial Services, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House says Congress must refuse to give extra funding or special regulatory help to companies or banks that are in trouble because of the AI market’s stress. Instead, the focus should be on helping all Americans who have been harmed.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 aims to establish standards and regulations that ensure AI systems are developed and tested in a reliable, safe, and trustworthy manner. It focuses on fostering responsible AI research, setting quality benchmarks, and protecting users and society from potential harms.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 is a proposed law that requires the Department of Veterans Affairs to disclose how it uses AI technologies, ensuring veterans and the public can understand the decision‑making processes behind AI‑driven services. It establishes standards for documentation, audits, and public reporting of AI systems used in VA programs to promote accountability and trust.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act is a proposed law that aims to ensure that the artificial‑intelligence tools used to evaluate and process veterans’ claims are fair, transparent, and reliable. It would set standards for how these AI systems are developed, monitored, and corrected so that veterans receive accurate decisions and have recourse if mistakes occur.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act is designed to shield people from misleading or deceptive practices by AI systems. It requires clear labeling of AI-generated content, sets transparency standards for developers, and establishes penalties for companies that mislead consumers about the nature or capabilities of their AI products.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act aims to strengthen national security by ensuring that AI systems are robust against cyber threats and malicious use. It establishes guidelines and standards for developing, deploying, and monitoring AI technologies to protect critical infrastructure and sensitive data.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act creates a dedicated task force within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to focus on the security of artificial intelligence systems. This task force will develop guidelines, standards, and best practices to protect critical infrastructure from AI-related threats and help maintain national security.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026 sets out national standards for assessing and reducing risks posed by AI systems, requiring developers to implement safeguards and conduct security audits. It also creates oversight bodies and reporting obligations to ensure transparency and accountability throughout the AI development and deployment lifecycle.

title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026 creates a national framework to regulate, oversee, and coordinate the development and deployment of AI‑driven physical systems such as autonomous vehicles, drones, and robotics. It establishes standards, safety protocols, and an interagency oversight body to ensure these systems operate responsibly and transparently.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: This policy aims to safeguard elections by limiting the use of AI systems that can spread misinformation or manipulate voter perceptions. It establishes rules and oversight mechanisms to prevent deceptive AI tools from influencing the democratic process.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self‑Improving AI Monitoring Act is a law that sets rules for overseeing artificial intelligence systems that can learn and adapt on their own. It requires regular checks, reporting, and safeguards to ensure these self‑improving technologies operate safely, transparently, and in an accountable manner.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act is proposed legislation that aims to prevent autonomous AI systems from acting outside human control, reducing potential harm to society. It would establish regulatory frameworks, safety standards, and oversight mechanisms to keep AI behavior aligned with legal and ethical guidelines.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary pause on the construction of new AI data centers to address environmental, energy, and societal concerns. It aims to encourage a careful assessment of impacts before expanding AI infrastructure, ensuring sustainable and responsible development.

title: Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026 creates a federal board tasked with monitoring, investigating, and regulating the intersection of artificial intelligence and cybersecurity threats. The act requires companies to report AI‑related security incidents and establishes guidelines for cooperation with the board to protect critical infrastructure and consumer data.

title: Make AI Work for Americans Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The “Make AI Work for Americans Act” is a proposed law designed to ensure that artificial intelligence technologies are developed and used in ways that benefit American people. It aims to set guidelines, oversight, and incentives that prioritize public safety, privacy, and economic advantage for U.S. citizens.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: China’s AI Power Report Act requires companies and organizations developing or deploying AI systems to track and publicly disclose their energy consumption and carbon footprint. The law aims to increase transparency, promote greener AI practices, and help the government gauge and reduce the sector’s overall environmental impact.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 makes it illegal to use artificial intelligence to diagnose, treat, or manage patients in medical settings, requiring that all clinical decisions be made by licensed physicians. The act aims to safeguard patient safety and uphold professional accountability by ensuring doctors, not machines, are responsible for medical care.

title: To establish the Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the Executive Office of the President, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: This policy aims to set up an Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats inside the President’s Executive Office. The office will monitor and address risks from AI and new technologies to protect national security and guide federal policy.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: The resolution formally establishes a Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence to oversee and guide the nation's AI policy. It aims to create a dedicated group that will study AI developments, assess risks, and recommend regulations to promote responsible use of artificial intelligence.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. Hearings held.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 establishes a legal framework for identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks associated with AI systems. It requires organizations that develop or deploy AI to conduct systematic risk evaluations and report their findings to regulatory authorities.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a proposed law aimed at establishing a comprehensive framework for regulating artificial intelligence. It seeks to ensure AI systems are safe, transparent, and respect fundamental rights.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 establishes guidelines for the creation and use of artificial intelligence systems to reduce their environmental footprint. It requires developers to conduct environmental impact assessments, implement energy‑efficient algorithms, and report their carbon emissions to ensure sustainable AI deployment.
